NextItNet stacks residual causal dilated convolutions; retained items matter through their relative offsets and convolutional paths, even without explicit position embeddings. For stride-one layers, maximum receptive-field span is R = 1 + Σℓ(kℓ−1)dℓ, counting every convolution inside residual blocks; exact reachable offsets depend on the dilation schedule. [NextItNet paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163). Architectural implication: deleting items, compacting survivors and left-padding again shifts each retained token right by the number of deleted tokens originally after it. This shrinks its lag to the final readout, changes adjacency and convolutional paths, and can bring previously unreachable items into coverage. Deletion therefore measures content removal plus temporal compression.

Position-preserving replacement keeps original slots and the readout anchor fixed, preserving structural receptive-field membership while changing content. However, interior PAD tokens differ from ordinary left-padding. A zero embedding does not guarantee zero intermediate activations: convolutional biases, normalization and neighboring inputs can produce signals unless masking explicitly suppresses them. Inspect the actual implementation; a newly introduced mask token is also untrained unless seen during training. These cautions follow from the [causal convolution implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html). Read the final nonpadding position, never nonpadding-count minus one; preferably retain the terminal item in controlled comparisons.

Recommended controls: compare targeted deletion against repeated random deletions matched for count, recency/lag bins, contiguous-run structure and terminal-item handling; compare targeted replacement against equivalently matched random replacements using the identical replacement rule. Report paired score/rank changes, uncertainty, position shifts and receptive-field membership changes. Treat these as intervention sensitivity, not isolated causal importance: compression and replacement can both create distribution shifts. [Hase et al.](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/hash/1def1713ebf17722cbe300cfc1c88558-Abstract.html) show removal-based explanations can reflect OOD behavior and replacement choice.
